subject: Next steps & safety probes: HealthGrid pilot proposal

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps & safety probes: HealthGrid pilot proposal

Hi Samir — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can get a small pilot scoped and running: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use: triage assistant for clinical intake forms (symptom ingestion + suggested next steps)
- Traffic: ~3k daily sessions initially, 1–2 concurrent requests typical, spikes to 50 during peak hours
- Must-haves: strict refusal on suicidal ideation and PHI extraction guardrails, audit logs for every request, and SOC 2 evidence for procurement

Recommended models & immediate tradeoffs
- redwood-7b-std (quantized q4f): best latency/cost balance for early pilot — typical 200-token run ~60–90ms p99 on our Dedicated nodes
- redwood-13b-guarded (fp16): stronger refusal behavior out of the box but ~2x token cost; recommended if you want stricter policy alignment at pilot start
- open-llama-30b-rlhf (quantized): if you need higher recall for clinical phrasing; expect higher latency and memory needs

Safety/refusal plan (short):
- We will run a focused refusal probe suite (attached safety_probe_matrix_v1.xlsx) that includes suicidal ideation, medication hallucination, and PII extraction cases
- Prompt-level guardrails: we propose the two-step prompt wrapper (attached prompt set) that enforces refusal templates and structured refusal codes for downstream logging

Attachments & links
- Attached: healthgrid_prompt_set_v1.json (seed prompts + wrapper logic), safety_probe_matrix_v1.xlsx, benchmark_latency_summary.csv
- Benchmark CSV and prompt examples: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/healthgrid/prompt-sets/healthgrid_prompt_set_v1

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Security: start your security questionnaire (we can pre-fill the SOC 2 pages) — I can send our audit pack once you confirm
2) Pilot scope: 2-week integration + 4-week pilot (sandbox) — suggested dates: 2027-06-07 start
3) Technical kick-off: engineering sync next Wed — can you confirm an hour slot?
4) Commercial: loop in Ben for pilot pricing and PO flow (cc'd)

If that looks good I'll schedule the technical call and drop the HubSpot mutual action plan entry. Any immediate questions on the model choices or the safety probes?

Thanks,
Olga
Principal Solutions Engineer

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>

Hi Samir, Elena — quick answers below and a proposed technical approach.

Latency details
- The 60–90ms p99 number was measured on our Dedicated nodes in us-west with batching disabled and a 200-token context. For hosted (multi-tenant) numbers expect ~120–220ms p99 depending on concurrency and model choice. We will instrument end-to-end traces in the console so you can validate p99 after integration.
- If the p99 needs to be <200ms for user-facing calls, redwood-7b-std (quantized) should meet that in Dedicated with continuous batching disabled; we recommend enabling prefix KV cache for repeated clinical forms to shave 15–30ms.

Refusal template (example)
- Prompt wrapper forces the model to return a structured JSON refusal when trigger phrases are detected. Example output: {"refusal_code": "SUICIDAL_IDEA", "message": "I can't help with that. If you or someone else is in immediate danger, please contact your local emergency services."} 
- The wrapper also emits the matched probe id for audit logging. We attached examples in healthgrid_prompt_set_v1.json (see the refusal_examples section).

Probe & evaluation plan
- Step 1 (week 0): baseline run of 500 probe cases across trigger categories (attached matrix)
- Step 2 (week 1): tuning of prompt guardrails and small model variant A/B to measure false accept/reject rates
- Step 3 (week 2–4): pilot traffic with live monitoring and regression alerts tied to guardrail probes

Proposed engineering kickoff
- Two 45min sessions: integration (auth, logging, telemetry) and safety probes (how tests are executed and interpreted). Proposed slots: Wed 2027-05-12 10:00 or 15:00 PT — which works for you?

I will also drop the benchmark CSV mentioned earlier — it lists token-level cost and median/90/99 latencies across the models we discussed.

Thanks,
Olga
